newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Solartech seen in HK$150 mln IPO - sources.
newsitem.headline: HK's Solartech seen in HK$150 mln IPO - sources.

text.p: Cable maker and exporter Solartech International Holdings Ltd is expected to issue 125 million new shares at HK$1.20 each in an initial public offering (IPO) of shares in Hong Kong, market sources said on Wednesday.

The new issue, representing 25 percent of the company's enlarged share capital, is expected at a price giving a fully-diluted price to earnings (P.E.) multiple of 7.79 times and a weighted average P.E. of 6.45 times, sources said.
A bonus issue of one warrant is expected to be attached for every five shares susbcribed, they added.

The IPO is expected to run from December 2 to 5 and dealing in the company shares is expected to begin on December 12, sources said. Lippo Secuities is seen to be the sponsor of the issue, they added.
Solartech produces cables and wires for electrical appliances and telecommunications products. It also makes power supply cords, telephone cords and video and audio cables.
Of the HK$136 million net proceeds expected to be raised, HK$35 million will be used to expand manufacturing facilitites, and HK$30 million to buy new machinery, sources said.
HK$35 million will be used to fund a bare copper rod making joint venture in China, HK$16 million for enlarging its customer network and the balance for working capital, they said.
The company reported profit of HK$42 million for the year ended March 31, 1996, on turnover of HK$453 million, up from HK$30 million on HK$396 million turnover in 1995, sources said.
Solartech posted a profit of HK$30 million on turnover of HK$156 million in the four months to July 31, 1996, they added.
"The company said its profit would increase to HK$45 million for the six months period (ended in September 30)," said an analyst who attended a Solartech presentation on Wednesday.

"It said that strong earnings growth in the past few months resulted from a drop in copper and PVC prices, and a change in product mix to products which carry higher profit margins," another analyst said.
